questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was a city that was nice to live in for exchange students. Other exchange students had had good experiences here. 
Prague is very much an Erasmus city and you can really feel that while you are there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Our Erasmus coordinator wrote me already before I came there and she was very quick to get back to you if you had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I came to Prague between 2-3 before I had to start school. Therefore I had a lot of time on "my own" before I got involved with the university. But I had found a flatshare with other exchange students before I arrived. So already the day I arrived I was surrounded by exchange students and we helped each other out. Otherwise the introduction days in the university they help you with getting in touch with a doctor, student ID, transportationpasses (where to buy) etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I would not say easy nor difficult. There is a webpage called erasmusinprague (they are a company that both hosts losts of events for erasmus students but another department also rent out flats for erasmus students). However it is a bit expensive (not more than at home) but compared to other prices in prague it is more expensive. I paid somewhere between 3900-4000 DKK. 
Our flat (a flatshare for 8 erasmus people) was an erasmusinprague flat. I did not find it through the web page though but through a facebook group for exchange students looking for accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Some of my friends lived on campus and I am very happy I did not. The dorms I have been in are further out of the city and they are very old and not well maintained. Furthermore the kitchens are very very small. And you had to bring a lot of kitchen stuff yourself. And you share a room. I would definitely  recommend finding flatshare. There are a lot of flatshares in prague it is just about being quick enough to get one from the erasmusinprague or find flatmates in the facebookgroups.

However!! Be careful finding flats outside of the erasmusinprague regi, I know three people who were scammed and had already paid.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I am not very good with the deadlines concerning registration and so on. So I am really not the right person to ask with questions like this. I don't even remember to be honest. Also because our erasmus coordinator at Charles University was so nice, so I feel like it could never go really wrong. Always help to get.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus Coordinator Lenka. So sweet.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
There are two weeks in the beginning of the semester where you can sign up for new courses and drop other. The add/drop period. This was so nice!! I had actually expected it to be very stressful but I was so happy it was possible because I ended having completely different courses than the courses I had had preapproved with KU. 
For me the workload of the courses was very important since I was mostly there to have fun and have the erasmus experience. Therefore I did not want to have courses with too heavy workloads and this was possible to avoid because of the add/drop period.
I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not stress before hand. In the add/drop period make sure you sign up/check when some of the classes you might want have available spots. In these two weeks I was checking in often to make sure I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine. I was not there for the academic part and therefore I did not choose hardcore academic courses either.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Wrong person to ask haha. I had some pretty easy going courses because that is what I was looking for. I could have taken higher level courses though.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Attendance is mandatory with often 2 absences allowed per class. 
I had to get used to this being so different from back home. 
More seminars and less lectures.
More courses than in DK because the courses are 'worth' fewer points.
In some courses mid-terms.
The final grade depends on your attendance, participation, midterms or papers during the semester (sounds like a lot but it is not) and final paper. This feels more like high school in Denmark. But it was really okay even though it sounds like a lot it was not at all.

I would definitely recommend checking out courses at other faculties than your own. I was in faculty of humanities but a lot of my courses were also in faculty in social sciences.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender and religion (6 ects)
Observing the city (3 ects)
World of documentary film (5 ects)
Iconology: Art-historical and philosophical aspects of reading the cultural phenomena (5 ects)
Cities in civilisation (3 ects)
Prague as a living city (6 ects)
Yoga (2 ects)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Observing the city. Our teacher michal was so nice and engaged. You get to do three mini fieldworks in the city where you focus on fx appropriation of space. I liked the course, I felt like I learned something and the teacher was so nice!

If you want easy courses:
Both iconology and cities in civilisation only require your attendance and nothing else! You literally only have to show up: no reading or final paper. 
Iconology was really difficult to understand though. I think you need some philosophy / art historical background in order to understand (I did not understand a lot). But the teacher was sweet!

World of documentary film: Also very nice teacher.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
If I have written 0 it is because I dont know how much I spent on this specific one!
I was very 'free' with my money. I did not care that much because I was like, now we are here, lets go.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transportation is very cheap when you buy the passes and especially the student passes.
Everything is just cheaper than in Denmark. Food, beer, drinks, the cinema etc.
I think a cinema ticket was 40 DKK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
This was not really something you get through the university in Prague. Or maybe I just did not know or seek it out. There are two companies working to make events for erasmus students. Erasmusinprague and Ohmyprague. Both host a lot of parties but they also host city tours, beach volley, basketball, soccer events etc and then you can just agree to play every x-day fx. 
I used these opportunities a lot in the beginning when I did not know anybody and uni had not started yet. It was a good way to get in contact with other erasmus students. Later on I did not use it as much, when I had met my friends.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Again not through the institution (maybe!!). 
I had yoga as a course and there were some sport courses you could get ects for.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Beach volley with erasmusinprague or ohmyprague is very nice especially in the beginning when it is warmer. I only stopped going because I dislocated my shoulder. 
A lot of people meet outside to play something no matter what level you are.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Vienna, Bratislava etc is not that far away. I had weekendtrips to Vienna, Budapest, Berlin, Brno it was nice to go on trips with the friends I made there. 
I would not recommend going to Pilsen, it was very boring. Maybe also not Brno (in good weather I think it is nicer than when I was there).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Czech people are not so welcoming people but I think they are quite funny. Even though they consider themselves to be centraleuropeans they really have that oldschool (especially the older generation) kind of harsh/closed of (sometimes rude service) but then there are also the really nice ones and then when you get good service you really appreciate it haha. Now I think I made them sound too harsh they are not. 
It was very easy although sometimes the language barriere can be big (not always). 
I felt very home in Prague in a short amount of time.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: To be honest I did not really do this. I think it is a lot like with erasmus students here in DK they often keep to themselves because they are there for a limited amount of time and dont know anybody and need a social circle so they are really in the same position and then it is really easy to find each other. However with that said I think you could actually quite easy socialize with czech students if you want to. I just did not seek it out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Language barriere: you find out that in Denmark we are actually really good in english. 
Maybe the closed off ness I wrote about earlier. But I did not really find any of this particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I love how much Czech people love beer (most beer consuming country in the world). Even though the food is not that good (very much sovs og kartofler (brød dumplings) I really miss it. The food, especially in the canteen, is just gravy, pork and dumplings and it is not really good but I miss it so much!! It's part of it.
I miss trams!! So good transportation system in Prague. I miss their attitude, the grey Czech cuisine, the beer, the prices (!!!!!), and that everything is so old.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find a flatshare with other exchange students. My flatshare has had a massive impact on my experience. 

2. I have been the type to have a lot of friends in school and be around in an exchange community like the one in Prague. But this time I was very determined to find a 'few' 'right' people for me. I have 8 really close friends with me home. I did almost everything with these people. They are my whole stay. 

3. Don't let the money stop you. You can always earn them back later. And it is Czech Republic so stuff is kinda cheap (not crazy cheap but cheaper than DK) which means you can actually "live" so much more here, because your money gets you further - enjoy that!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really anything I can think of that I have not mentioned already.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The most rewarding part of my exchange is 100 % the friends I made there.
I have really gotten everything I wanted from my exchange in Prague.

Originally I was going to Melbourne in Australia so suddenly it was something very different than I had expected my whole exchange experience to be like. But I would not change it for the world. I have gotten so close friends, cliche but really friends for life. We are still in contact and travelling around europe this spring/summer to visit each other. I love and miss them so much.
 
My experience is actually that when you go on exchange inside Europe you have more international friends compared to going overseas to fx Canada or Australia here you definitely have some but most of your friend group is danish (from what I can see with my friends!). And I am so happy I have close friends in France, Netherlands, Norway etc now (even though it is hard too). 

And beside all of this: Prague is really a great city to live in. It is so beautiful and old, and with lots of opportunities.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To not drink too much when the beer was so cheap. No I don't really know. For me probably having a shoulder injury while abroad.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Prague!! I was not expecting a lot because I was sad for a long time about not going to Australia and I really feel like I have had the best possible experience I could have had.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
